intro: This lesson brings together the key points of level A1 (lessons 1 to 39) in clear tables, then gives you a mixed test to check what you know before you start level A2.
objectifs: Review the basic forms: to be (present and past), have got, present simple and present continuous.
Review determiners and quantity: a / an / the, plurals, possessives, some / any, how much / how many.
Review prepositions of place and time, the time and dates.
Review questions, can, the imperative, would like, like + -ing and linking words.
See what you know well and what you need to practise again.

sections.titre: 1. “To be” in the present and the past
texte: Use “to be” for identity, age, feelings, place and weather (lessons 1, 4 and 39). Don't use “do / did” with “to be”: put the verb before the subject in questions.
Remember: I'm 25 (not “I have 25 years”); It's cold (you need the subject “it”); I was born in 1998.

lignes: I was / you were / he was / we were / they were
I'm not / he isn't / they aren't
Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.
Yes, I was. / No, they weren't.

exemples: Are you a student? — No, I'm not. I'm a nurse.
Where were you yesterday? — I was at home.

sections.titre: 2. Present simple, present continuous, have got
texte: Present simple (lesson 6): habits and facts; s with he / she / it; do / does for questions and negatives. Adverbs of frequency (lesson 7) go before the main verb: I usually get up at 7.
Present continuous (lessons 8 and 9): an action happening now; be + verb-ing. “Have got” (lesson 5): possession, mostly in British English.
exemples: I usually take the bus, but today I'm walking.

texte: a / an before a singular countable noun (a car, an hour); the for a specific thing; no article for things in general (I like music) (lesson 11). Irregular plurals: children, people, men, women (lesson 12).
this / these (near), that / those (far) (lesson 13); my, your, his, her, its, our, their (lesson 14); possessive ’s: my sister's car, my parents' house (lesson 15).
Quantity (lessons 30 and 31): some in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions; how many + plural, how much + uncountable; there is / there are (lesson 16).

lignes: his = of a man, her = of a woman
How much money? How many people?
money is uncountable, people is plural

exemples: How many children have they got? — Three.

sections.titre: 4. Place, time, the clock and dates
texte: Place (lesson 17): in, on, under, next to, between, opposite, behind, in front of. Time (lesson 18): at + clock time, on + day / date, in + month / year / season.
The time (lesson 21): It's half past seven / a quarter to eight / seven forty-five. Dates (lesson 22): the fourteenth of November, with an ordinal number.

lignes: on the table, on the left

exemples: The meeting is on Tuesday at half past nine.
My keys are on the table, next to the phone.

sections.titre: 5. Questions, can, imperative, would like, like + -ing
texte: Wh- questions (lesson 29): question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Where do you live?). Can (lesson 28): + verb with no to, no do. Imperative (lesson 32): verb alone, Don't + verb, Let's + verb.

Like / love / hate + -ing (lesson 33) for tastes; would like + to (lesson 34) for polite requests. Linking words (lesson 36): and, but, because, or. Adjectives (lesson 35): before the noun, never change.

lignes: What time does the film start?
Can you swim? — Yes, I can.
Turn left. Don't be late. Let's go!
I'd like a coffee. I'd like to go home.
I'm tired because I work at night, but I'm happy.

exemples: Why are you learning English? — Because I'd like to work in Canada.
I like dancing, but I can't sing at all.

texte: Do the test below without looking at the tables, then check your answers. For each mistake, write the number of the lesson and read it again.

If you get at least 80% right, you are ready for level A2, which starts with the past simple of regular verbs (lesson 41). If not, first review “to be”, the present simple and questions: they are the base of everything else.

formule: be · have got · present simple / continuous · a / an / the · some / any · at / on / in · Wh- + auxiliary + subject + verb · can · Don't… · I'd like to… · like + -ing · was / were
prononciation: Short and weak forms: I'm, it's, can /kən/, was /wəz/; but strong forms in short answers: Yes, I CAN. Yes, I WAS.
The s of he / she / it and of plurals: /s/ (works, cats), /z/ (plays, dogs), /ɪz/ (watches, buses).
th: /ð/ in this, the, they, mother; /θ/ in think, three, fourth. Tongue between the teeth.
Stress in numbers: thirTEEN / THIRty, fifTEEN / FIFty.
Intonation: down for Wh- questions (Where do you LIVE? ↘), up for yes / no questions (Are you READY? ↗).
erreurs: s with he / she / it in the present simple (lesson 6).

dialogue.contexte: In Montreal, the last A1 class. The teacher, Mrs Gagnon, talks with Ibrahima, a student from Senegal.
lignes: So, Ibrahima, this is our last A1 class. How was the course?
How was…? = asking for an opinion.
It was great! At the start I wasn't very confident, but now I can speak a little.
What do you like doing in English?
I love watching videos and I often listen to podcasts on the bus.
Very good. And what's difficult for you?
That's normal. Practise a little every day. Would you like some extra exercises?
Yes, please! And when does the A2 course start?
Accepting an offer; does in the question.
On Monday the 7th of December, at half past six.

mots: do something again and again to get better (US: practice)
how good you are at something
questions to check what you know
sure about yourself and your abilities

items: We (was / were) in Lyon last week.
(How much / How many) water do you drink?
___ you speak French? — Yes, I can.
Is ___ any milk in the fridge?
This is Anna. ___ husband is a doctor.
I'd like ___ book a table, please.
___ be late! The train leaves at eight.

exercices.consigne: Complete with at, on or in.
Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: He have got a new car.
He has got a new car. / He's got a new car.
What is your sister doing usually at the weekend?
What does your sister usually do at the weekend?
I haven't got any money. / I don't have any money.
The children of my brother are funny.

exercices.consigne: Write the English sentence for each situation.
items: Say you want food and you feel cold.
Ask someone their country or town of origin.
Ask politely for a glass of water.
I'd like a glass of water, please.
Say you don't like shopping and give the reason: it's tiring.
I don't like shopping because it's tiring.

exercices.consigne: Introduce yourself in six to eight sentences: name, age, town, family, job or studies, a habit, what you are doing at the moment, what you like doing, what you can do, and where you were last weekend.
items: Hi, I'm Clarisse. I'm 27 and I live in Yaoundé. I've got two brothers and a sister. I'm a nurse and I work in a big hospital. I usually start work at seven o'clock. At the moment I'm learning English because I'd like to work in Canada. I love dancing and I can cook very well. Last weekend I was in Kribi with my friends, and the weather was beautiful.

a_retenir: “To be” for age, feelings, weather: I'm 30, I'm hungry, It's cold; in the past: was / were.
Present simple for habits (s with he / she / it, do / does); present continuous for now (be + -ing).
Questions: question word + auxiliary + subject + verb; can and be don't use “do”.
some / any, how much / how many, there is / there are, at / on / in: small words make a big difference.
Politeness: I'd like…, Can I…?, please; tastes: I love + -ing.
